results.title: interest rates essay (Maxim)
results.known: 24–25 out of 25, per the examiner (a real confirmed range, not a single invented number — deliberately kept as a range here rather than forced to one figure).

issues.text: The statement ‘interest rates only increase the cost of borrowing, does not therefore reduced disposable incomes of consumers’ is inaccurate and weakens the theoretical explanation.

results.improvement: Correct the claim about disposable income by explaining that higher interest rates raise debt‑service costs, reducing real disposable income and thus reinforcing the consumption channel.

results.title: monopoly efficiency essay (Seb)
results.known: 21 out of 25, marked by his teacher (confirmed with George 2026-08-12 — not Seb's own self-assessment, which was the thing worth ruling out given Seb's interview describes him self-marking).

issues.text: "produce even AC and still make SNP (P−C×Q)" misstates X‑inefficiency, which should be production above the minimum AC.

results.improvement: Revise the sentence to read: "A monopoly may produce above the minimum average cost (X‑inefficiency) and still earn a profit (P‑C)\u00D7Q," thereby correcting the definition of X‑inefficiency.

results.title: carbon emissions / road traffic essay
results.known: 22 out of 25. Marker not yet specified — confirm whether this was a teacher or an examiner before treating it as a firm anchor (same standard applied to Test 2).

issues.text: The statement that "MPC=MSC, thus shifting behaviour to switch (MPC + tax) fully internalising the DWL" misrepresents the effect of a tax, which raises private marginal cost to equal marginal social cost rather than equating MPC and MSC without the tax.

results.improvement: Clarify the tax mechanism by stating that the tax raises the private marginal cost (MPC) so that MPC + tax = MSC, thereby internalising the external cost.

results.title: National Minimum Wage / social care essay
results.known: 19–20 out of 25, marked by the teacher (confirmed with George 2026-08-13). Originally reported only as "mid A", which is a grade band rather than a mark — the real figure was obtained rather than inferred from a grade boundary, since guessing it and then treating the guess as ground truth is exactly the substitution this project exists to prevent. Kept as a range, which is honest, rather than forced to one number.

issues.text: ‘...instead just produce at (PQ) where MPC is less than MSC.’ – the inequality is reversed, misrepresenting the externality relationship.
‘However, due to higher wages this may increase worker motivation and thus lead to higher productivity.’ – the causal link is asserted without explanation or evidence.
Diagram description list (e.g., ‘Firm cost/revenue diagram: AR and MR curves…’) is not referenced or integrated into the essay’s analysis.

results.improvement: Replace the sentence ‘...where MPC is less than MSC’ with ‘...where MPC is greater than MSC’, correcting the externality relationship and briefly note that this implies a negative externality and a welfare loss.

issues.text: The Dutch disease paragraph ends abruptly with "Dutch disease is a downside of [TEXT MISSING — cut off by page break]" leaving the explanation incomplete.

results.improvement: Extend the Dutch disease paragraph (e.g., after "This appreciation causes other sectors…") to fully explain how currency appreciation reduces competitiveness, lowers manufacturing output and can offset growth gains, providing a clearer evaluation of its impact.
